title: Expansion of British Power in India

notes.subtopic: 1. Big Picture — Wars and Policies of Expansion
notes.content:
**Executive summary:** After the Carnatic Wars, Plassey and Buxar, the British became a major power. The **Marathas, Mysore and the Nizam** fought each other for the Deccan; the British joined in to become the **dominant power**. They expanded through **wars** (Anglo-Mysore, Anglo-Maratha, Anglo-Sikh) and **policies** (Subsidiary Alliance, Doctrine of Lapse, annexation for maladministration).

| Wars | Number | Period | Ended with |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anglo-Mysore | 4 | 1767–1799 | Tipu killed at Seringapatam |
| Anglo-Maratha | 3 | 1775–1818 | Peshwaship abolished |
| Anglo-Sikh | 2 | 1845–1849 | Punjab annexed |

**Why the British won:** **disunity** among Indian states + superior **military and financial resources**.

fiveW.who: Hyder Ali (and Tipu) vs the British, with the Nizam and Marathas switching sides
fiveW.where: Mysore, Carnatic — Arcot, Porto Novo, Mahe
fiveW.what: First two wars to subdue Mysore
fiveW.why: Rise of Mysore threatened British expansion; British seized Mahe
fiveW.how: Alliances and counter-alliances; Hyder's diplomacy; treaties of Salbai and Mangalore

notes.content:
**Hyder Ali** — efficient administrator, diplomat and general; Mysore's rise threatened the EEIC.

**First Anglo-Mysore War (1767–69)**
• British allied with the **Nizam and the Marathas** against Hyder.
• Hyder, a great **diplomat**, won them over → **crushing defeat for the British**.

**Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780–84)**
• **Cause:** British occupied the French port of **Mahe** (under Hyder's jurisdiction) and stopped Mysore's trade with Europe.
• Mysore + Marathas + Nizam captured **Arcot**.
• **Treaty of Salbai (1782)** — Marathas withdrew support.
• Hyder **defeated at Porto Novo**; died — **Tipu Sultan** continued.
• Ended by the **Treaty of Mangalore (1784)**.

fiveW.who: Tipu Sultan vs the British (Cornwallis, then Wellesley), Marathas and Nizam
fiveW.what: Defeat and death of Tipu; end of Mysore's independence
fiveW.why: Tipu attacked Travancore (1789) and refused the Subsidiary Alliance
fiveW.how: Treaty of Seringapatam 1792; final siege of Seringapatam 1799

notes.content:
**Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790–92)**
• **Cause:** Tipu attacked **Travancore (1789)** — a British ally and **pepper** supplier.
• British allied with the Marathas and Nizam; Tipu defeated.
• **Treaty of Seringapatam (1792):** Tipu gave up **large territory**, paid a **huge fine**, sent **two sons as hostages**.

**Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1798–99)**
• Tipu built a large army to avenge his defeat; **refused Lord Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance**.
• **Tipu died defending Seringapatam (1799)**.
• **Half of Mysore** divided between the British and the **Nizam**; the other half returned to the **old Raja (Wodeyar)** family.

**Result:** it took **30+ years** to subdue Mysore; British territory stretched from the **Malabar to the Coromandel Coast**.

fiveW.who: Marathas (Nana Phadnavis, Baji Rao II, Scindias, Holkars, Bhonsles) vs the British (Wellesley)
fiveW.where: Maharashtra and central India — Salsette, Bassein, Poona, Kirkee
fiveW.what: Three wars that ended Maratha power
fiveW.why: Maratha succession disputes and disunity gave the British openings
fiveW.how: Supporting rival claimants; Subsidiary Alliance; defeat at Kirkee

notes.content:
**Background:** 1773 — **Peshwa Narayan Rao murdered**; succession war between infant **Madhav Rao II** (guided by **Nana Phadnavis**) and **Raghunath Rao (Raghoba)**.

**First (1775–82):** Raghoba sought British help, promising **Salsette and Bassein**. Marathas under Nana Phadnavis defeated the British; no decisive result → **Treaty of Salbai (1782)** → 20 years of peace.

**Second (1803–05):** after Madhav Rao II's death (1796), weak **Baji Rao II** became Peshwa; **Nana Phadnavis died** → infighting. **1802** — Holkars defeated the Peshwa and the Scindias → Peshwa signed the **Subsidiary Alliance** (Treaty of Bassein) with **Wellesley**. **Scindias and Bhonsles** fought (1803), lost, and accepted the Alliance.

**Third (1817–18):** Baji Rao II, with Holkars and Bhonsles, attacked the **British Residency at Kirkee** — completely defeated.

**Results:** Baji Rao II **exiled to Bithur** (near Kanpur) with a pension; **Peshwaship ended**; Maratha lands annexed; small **Satara** state for a descendant of **Shivaji**.

fiveW.who: Sikhs (after Ranjit Singh) vs the British — Lord Hardinge, Lord Dalhousie
fiveW.what: Two wars leading to the annexation of Punjab
fiveW.why: Punjab was essential for the British Empire; chaos after Ranjit Singh's death
fiveW.how: Sikhs crossed the Sutlej; treachery within; Treaty of Lahore; Dalhousie annexed Punjab

notes.content:
• **Treaty of Amritsar (1809)** with Ranjit Singh — **Sutlej** as boundary.
• After his death (1839) his system broke down; the **Sikh army** took charge → British saw a chance.

**First Anglo-Sikh War (1845–46)**
• Sikhs **crossed the Sutlej** (violating the treaty); **Lord Hardinge** attacked.
• Sikhs lost due to **treachery of their own men** (Raja Lal Singh led the Sikh forces).
• **Treaty of Lahore (1846)**.

**Second Anglo-Sikh War (1848–49)**
• Resentment at British control → revolts.
• **Lord Dalhousie** crushed the Sikh army and **annexed Punjab (1849)**.

**Results:** **Maharaja Dalip Singh** (Ranjit Singh's son) pensioned and sent to **England**; British officers commanded the Sikh army. **Conquest of India complete.**

fiveW.who: Lord Wellesley, Governor-General; first signed by the Nizam of Hyderabad
fiveW.where: Indian princely states — Hyderabad, Awadh, Tanjore, Mysore, Peshwa, Scindia, Bhonsle…
fiveW.what: Alliance making Indian rulers dependent on the British
fiveW.why: To expand British dominion without direct war
fiveW.how: British troops stationed and paid for by the ruler; a Resident at court; foreign policy controlled

notes.content:
**Offer:** a ruler who felt threatened could ally with the British, who would **protect him from external attack and internal revolt**.

**Clauses**
• **British troops** stationed permanently in the state.
• A **British Resident** at the ruler's court.
• Ruler **paid for the troops** — in cash, kind, or by **ceding territory**.
• **No non-British Europeans** in his service.
• **No alliance** with any power without British consent.
• Ruler acknowledged British **dominion**.

| Advantages for British | Disadvantages for Indian rulers |
|---|---|
| Got territory as subsidy payment | Lost **independence** |
| Large armies maintained at the rulers' cost | States became **poor**; when administration collapsed, British annexed them |
| Kept other Europeans out of Indian courts | Rulers neglected their people's **welfare** |

**First to sign: the Nizam of Hyderabad.**

notes.subtopic: 7. Lord Dalhousie — Doctrine of Lapse and Annexation of Awadh

fiveW.who: Lord Dalhousie (Governor-General 1848–56); Wajid Ali Shah of Awadh
fiveW.what: Annexation of states without heirs and on grounds of 'maladministration'
fiveW.how: Adoption rights denied; Awadh annexed in 1856 for inept governance

notes.content:
**Doctrine of Lapse**
• If a ruler died **without a natural male heir**, the state **'lapsed' to the British**; **adoption not recognised**.
• Applied to **Jhansi, Nagpur, Satara**; rulers given pensions → deep **dissatisfaction** (a cause of 1857).

**Annexation on grounds of maladministration**
• **Awadh** had followed the Subsidiary Alliance faithfully.
• Dalhousie called Nawab **Wajid Ali Shah** incompetent and **annexed Awadh in 1856** for inept governance.
• **Irony:** Awadh's administrative failure was largely caused by the **Subsidiary Alliance** itself.

**By 1856–57** the British were the **paramount power** in India.

questions.answer: Wellesley-Subsidiary Alliance · Dalhousie-Lapse · Hardinge-First Sikh War

questions.question: (a) Causes of the First Anglo-Mysore War (b) Results of the Second (c) Policy introduced by Wellesley in the Fourth.
questions.answer:
• (a) The rise of Hyder Ali's Mysore threatened British expansion; the British allied with the Nizam and Marathas against him.
  • (b) Hyder was defeated at Porto Novo; Tipu continued; the war ended with the Treaty of Mangalore (1784) — no decisive result.
  • (c) Subsidiary Alliance — Tipu refused it, leading to war.

questions.question: Give two results of the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.
questions.answer:
• Tipu Sultan died defending his capital Seringapatam (1799).
  • Half of Mysore was divided between the British and the Nizam; the other half went back to the old Raja of Mysore.

questions.question: What was the Treaty of Salbai?
questions.answer: A peace treaty signed in 1782 between the British and the Marathas that ended the First Anglo-Maratha War; the Marathas also withdrew support from Hyder Ali. It brought 20 years of peace.

questions.question: Describe the three Anglo-Maratha Wars and their results.
questions.answer:
• First (1775–82): British backed Raghoba for Salsette and Bassein; Nana Phadnavis resisted; Treaty of Salbai.
  • Second (1803–05): weak Baji Rao II signed the Subsidiary Alliance (1802); Scindias and Bhonsles fought, lost, and accepted it.
  • Third (1817–18): Peshwa attacked the Residency at Kirkee; defeated.
  • Results: Peshwaship ended; Baji Rao II exiled to Bithur; lands annexed; Satara given to Shivaji's descendant.
questions.topperTip: Maratha disunity is the thread running through all three wars — say so.

questions.question: Name the Governor-General in the First Anglo-Sikh War. Why did it take place? When was Punjab annexed?
questions.answer:
• Lord Hardinge.
  • After Ranjit Singh's death the system collapsed and the Sikh army took charge; the Sikhs crossed the Sutlej, violating the Treaty of Amritsar, and the British attacked.
  • Punjab was annexed in 1849 by Lord Dalhousie after the Second Anglo-Sikh War.

questions.question: Who introduced the Subsidiary Alliance and why? What were its clauses?
questions.answer:
• Introduced by Lord Wellesley to expand British dominion without costly wars.
  • Clauses: British troops stationed permanently; a British Resident at court; ruler paid for troops (cash, kind or territory); no non-British Europeans employed; no alliances without British consent; ruler acknowledged British dominion.

questions.question: 'The Subsidiary Alliance adversely affected the Indian kingdoms.' Do you agree? How did the British benefit?
questions.answer:
Yes.

  • Rulers lost their independence.
  • Paying subsidies made states poor; when administration collapsed the British annexed them (e.g. Awadh).
  • Protected by the British, rulers ignored their people's welfare.

British gains: territory as payment; large armies at Indian expense; other Europeans kept out.

questions.question: (Picture) Governor-General who used an alliance policy: name the policy, the first ruler to join and its disadvantages.
questions.answer:
• (a) Subsidiary Alliance (Lord Wellesley).
  • (b) The Nizam of Hyderabad.
  • (c) Rulers lost independence; states became poor; people suffered as rulers neglected welfare; states were later annexed.

questions.question: What was the Doctrine of Lapse? Name two states annexed under it.
questions.answer: Policy of Lord Dalhousie: if a ruler of a dependent state died without a natural male heir, the state 'lapsed' to the British; adoption was not recognised. States annexed: Jhansi, Nagpur, Satara. It caused deep resentment among rulers.

questions.question: Why is the annexation of Awadh considered unjust?
questions.answer:
• Awadh had faithfully followed the Subsidiary Alliance.
  • Dalhousie annexed it in 1856 calling Nawab Wajid Ali Shah incompetent (maladministration).
  • But Awadh's administrative failure was largely caused by the Subsidiary Alliance itself — so the British punished the Nawab for a problem they created. This angered the people and sepoys of Awadh (a cause of 1857).
questions.topperTip: Pointing out the irony is what earns the HOTS mark.
